name: Cryptic crossword No 22,586
preamble: Eight solutions are of a kind and lack further definition.

clue.text: The grand manner gives God pain

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and wild places
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: A haughty, grandiose style of behaviour is said to cause the Almighty suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God' with a capital letter suggests the Almighty, but the setter wants a pagan deity, the goat-footed Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence of style, a dashing flourish in how someone carries themselves.

clue.text: One of one's kidneys is outside society

indicators.note: to be outside something is to surround it, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: 'one' as the indefinite article
renal is the adjective meaning of or relating to the kidneys
S is the standard abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Someone describes one of their kidneys as being cut off from society, a strange medical complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kidneys' looks like anatomy, but the clue wants the adjective, with the society letter slipped in after its first letter. The preamble's kind is London football clubs; Arsenal is the north London club at the Emirates Stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: There is no definition: the preamble says eight answers belong to one category, here London football clubs.

clue.text: Summer snake?

blocks.note: first meaning: one who sums, a person or machine that does addition
second meaning: the common viper of Britain and Europe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' reads as the hot season, as if this were a snake that comes out in warm weather; it is really someone who sums.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an agent noun for a person who totals figures and the name of Britain's only venomous reptile, the viper.

clue.text: See 7
Nothing but diamonds is right

blocks.note: 'just' means only, nothing but
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player insists that only the diamond suit is the correct lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamonds' suggests the card suit, but here it is the gems, which underworld slang calls ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Justice and right are both nouns for what is morally fair and lawful, as in 'to do someone right'.

clue.text: See 29
They're briefly won by a knight

blocks.note: surface reading: some unnamed things, mentioned in passing
setter's reading: the club's short name is Spurs, and a medieval knight was said to win his spurs when first proving himself

explanation.surface: Some unspecified prizes are said to be won by a chivalrous knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' means take the club's nickname, Spurs; 'to win one's spurs' is the old phrase for a knight earning his rank. The club's name also honours Harry Hotspur, a real medieval knight.
explanation.definitionFit: There is no definition: the preamble says eight answers belong to one category, here London football clubs.

clue.text: Provision of much else as well

indicators.note: what a phrase provides is contained in it, so the letters are supplied from within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of 'much', all of 'else' and the start of 'as'

explanation.surface: Someone is supplied with plenty, and other things besides.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span three words of the phrase. Chelsea is the west London club based at Stamford Bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: There is no definition: the preamble says eight answers belong to one category, here London football clubs.

clue.text: Repeatedly copy Milan fashion - that's how we mean to do business

definitions.text: that's how we mean to do business

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: the word taken twice, as 'repeatedly' asks
taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm admits its strategy is to keep imitating the designs of Milan's fashion houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milan fashion' looks like the Italian catwalk, but 'fashion' is a verb working on the letters of two copies plus the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A company policy is a firm's stated rule or practice, the official way it intends to operate.

clue.text: Accustomed to being exploited

blocks.note: first meaning: familiar with
second meaning: taken advantage of

explanation.surface: Someone has grown so familiar with being taken advantage of that they no longer notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, 'accustomed to being exploited', but splits into two meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The participle serves as an adjective meaning familiar with something and as a past form meaning manipulated or taken advantage of.

clue.text: Time off - tie went off

indicators.note: something that has gone off is spoiled or out of order, so these letters are disarranged

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter of the three words

explanation.surface: A break from work is announced as the moment a match ended level, or a tie fell off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time off' looks like a holiday; 'Time' alone is the definition and 'off' signals the rearrangement. The second 'off' is fodder, not a repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-fifteen is a clock reading, a particular moment of the day, so it is an example of a time.

clue.text: See what's in the parcel - bad pun about raw material

indicators.note: a bad version is a corrupted one, so the letters come out wrongly ordered
material is stuff waiting to be worked into shape, so these letters are reshaped
to be about something is to go around it, so one set of letters encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful joke is made about raw material while a parcel is being opened.
explanation.walkthrough: The two short words are each rearranged and one wraps around the other, a fitting device for a parcel clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwrap a package is to remove its covering so that its contents can be seen.

clue.text: Writer among peers with diversion that's intentional

indicators.note: a diversion sends things off their usual route, so the letters are rerouted
to be among others is to be placed inside them

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument, so a writer
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author sits in the House of Lords and causes a deliberate distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but crosswords often use it for the pen itself. Prepense survives mainly in the legal phrase 'malice prepense'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepense is an old legal adjective meaning planned beforehand, deliberate, as in malice aforethought.

clue.text: Excessively Scottish during brief affair's maturity

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits inside it, so one piece lies within another

blocks.note: a fling is a short romance
ower is the Scots form of 'over', meaning too much

explanation.surface: A Scot carries on a short romance far too intensely just as they reach adulthood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excessively Scottish' sounds like a description of someone; it asks for the Scots spelling of 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowering is the stage of full development or prime, the figurative blossoming of a person or culture.

clue.text: Mynheer Kok continued to lose vital fluid

blocks.note: Wim Kok was Dutch prime minister in the 1990s; mynheer is Dutch for 'mister'
to bleed is to lose blood
to go on is to continue

explanation.surface: A Dutch gentleman named Kok kept on losing blood.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dutch prime minister supplies his first name. Wimbledon FC was a south-west London club of the time, famed as the 'Crazy Gang'.
explanation.definitionFit: There is no definition: the preamble says eight answers belong to one category, here London football clubs.

clue.text: Fellow in the Cat and Fiddle

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
'he' stands for any male person

explanation.surface: A man is drinking in a pub called the Cat and Fiddle, named after the nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat and Fiddle' reads as one pub name; it splits into fodder and definition. A fiddle in British slang is a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle is to swindle or falsify accounts, so it is a synonym for dishonest trickery.

clue.text: Proceeded quietly through waterlogged area?

blocks.note: swam is the past of swim, to proceed through water
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone crept silently across a soggy marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeded quietly' looks like walking on tiptoe; the question mark admits that going through a bog would really mean swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: A swamp is a marsh or bog, land so saturated that it lies permanently wet.

clue.text: Review displaying pure wit

indicators.note: to display is to lay out for show, so the letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic's notice is full of nothing but cleverness.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the surface agree so well that the anagram indicator hides in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A write-up is a published article assessing something, such as a newspaper notice of a play.

clue.text: Semi-human beings entering at home

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
semi- means partly, so part
men as people generally

explanation.surface: Half-human creatures walk into a house, like a scene from a horror film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semi-human' looks like one word for a monster; the hyphen hides two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a set of rooms used as a dwelling, which is a place someone lives.

clue.text: One who decides about uncharged energy being put in

indicators.note: a thing put in goes inside something else

blocks.note: re is Latin for concerning
free of charge
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An arbiter must rule on whether neutral, uncharged energy has been added, a physics puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncharged' with 'energy' suggests electricity, but it means costing nothing. A referee also fits the theme, as the official in a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee is an arbiter whose rulings settle disputes, in sport or elsewhere.

clue.text: A painter gets a profit that rises and falls

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: An artist makes money on an investment that goes up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rises and falls' looks like a fluctuating market; 'rises' turns the letters upward and 'falls' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US–Canada border, so it is the name of some falls.

clue.text: The field where the ball should go?

blocks.note: surface reading: a playing field or pitch
setter's reading: a goal is a crossbar over a net, so the ball should go beneath the one into the other

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful reading: a goal's crossbar and net together give the club's name. Barnet is a north London borough and its football club.
explanation.definitionFit: There is no definition: the preamble says eight answers belong to one category, here London football clubs.

clue.text: It encloses the factory

blocks.note: a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill
a wall is what encloses a site

explanation.surface: A plain description of the boundary that surrounds an industrial works.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a plain description of a boundary, and the barrier around a mill is literally the answer. Millwall is the south-east London club known as the Lions.
explanation.definitionFit: There is no definition: the preamble says eight answers belong to one category, here London football clubs.

clue.text: Half - um - out?

indicators.note: out can mean out of order or not in place, so the letters are disarranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hesitant voice wonders whether someone is halfway out.
explanation.walkthrough: The hesitant 'um' looks like filler but is fodder. Fulham is the west London club at Craven Cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: There is no definition: the preamble says eight answers belong to one category, here London football clubs.

clue.text: The fields where time is short, none more so

blocks.note: leas are meadows, a poetic word for fields
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: On the land, work gets so hurried that nothing could be more so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time is short' sounds like a deadline; it asks for the abbreviation of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Least means to the smallest degree; something done least is done less than anything else, so nothing does it less.

clue.text: Transport union first bedecked with ribbons

definitions.text: Transport union first bedecked with ribbons

indicators.note: first means placed at the front, so one piece leads

blocks.note: a wedding is the union of a couple
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A vehicle for the bride and groom arrives draped in ribbons ahead of the ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport union' suggests a trade union for transport workers; the words split, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding car carries the bridal party and is traditionally decorated with white ribbons across the bonnet.

clue.text: A fashion on other grounds

blocks.note: taken as written
a fashion is a manner or method of doing something

explanation.surface: A style is adopted for some other reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On other grounds' reads as 'for other reasons', but here grounds are stadiums, so a team playing on the opponents' pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A side playing away competes at the opposing club's stadium rather than its own home pitch.

clue.text: Doctoring was corrosive and prickly

blocks.note: spin is doctoring the presentation of news, as a spin doctor does
acid ate away at the metal; to eat is to corrode

explanation.surface: Medical treatment proved harsh and thorny for the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctoring' suggests medicine; it is the political sense, spinning the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinate is a botanical word for bearing spines, so it describes a plant covered in sharp points.

clue.text: Was the organisation quiet about Ulster?

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange, so the letters are put into a new arrangement
to be about something is to surround it

blocks.note: taken as written
muted means hushed or quiet
NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a body kept silent about the troubles in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The organisation' looks like a group such as the IRA or UN, but 'organisation' signals the rearrangement. West Ham United is the east London club known as the Hammers.
explanation.definitionFit: There is no definition: the preamble says eight answers belong to one category, here London football clubs.
